name: Burg Starhemberg
kurzbeschreibung: Schloss Starkenberg near Tarrenz: built in 1310, historic Starkenberger Fehde, BierMythos adventure tour and castle brewery since 1810.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai–Okt täglich 10:00–17:00 Uhr, Nov–Apr Mo–Fr 10:00–16:00 Uhr
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Schloss Starkenberg (historically referred to in the records as Burg Starhemberg) rises on a sunny hill in the municipality of Tarrenz near Imst in the Tyrolean Oberland. Built in the early 14th century as Neu-Starkenberg, the castle complex formed the power center of the influential Tyrolean noble dynasty of the Lords of Starkenberg. Today, the castle combines medieval defensive architecture with living craft tradition: it houses the Schlossbrauerei Starkenberg, founded in 1810, and the popular adventure world Starkenberger BierMythos, which takes visitors deep into the historic castle vaults and the secrets of the brewing art.

History & Architecture

The defensive complex was built between 1310 and 1331 by the Herren von Starkenberg after their original ancestral seat, Alt-Starkenberg at the entrance to the Salvesenschlucht gorge, had become too small. In the early 15th century, the Starkenbergs ranked among the wealthiest noble families in the region. When they led the armed aristocratic uprising against the Tyrolean sovereign Herzog Friedrich IV. mit der leeren Tasche during the dramatic Starkenberger Fehde (1422–1426), ducal troops besieged the fortress. Friedrich IV. broke the supremacy of the dynasty; Neu-Starkenberg passed into princely territorial ownership and served henceforth as an administrative seat and regional court. In 1810, the Imst merchant Johann Carl Strele purchased the castle and established the castle brewery, which remains family-owned to this day. The historic building fabric includes a Romanesque-Gothic core, prominent defensive towers, winding courtyards, and Baroque castle wings. The 700-meter-long BierMythos adventure tour leads through 18 exhibition rooms spanning over 4,000 m² of exhibition space into the deep vaulted cellars, to the historic brewhouse, an ice cellar from the 16th century, and the former fermentation cellars.

Visit & Getting There

The BierMythos tour and the castle shop are open daily from 10:00 to 17:00 during the summer season (May to October). In the winter months (November to April), the tour is accessible Monday to Friday from 10:00 to 16:00 (closed on weekends and public holidays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €9.50 (including a small beer tasting at the bar), children aged 7 to 15 €6.50, children under 6 free; family ticket €25.00. The adjacent Starkenberger Schloss-Stube serves warm Tyrolean tavern cuisine from Tuesday to Sunday (closed on Mondays). Getting there by public transport: by train to Imst-Pitztal station, then take VVT bus route 4204 or 150 to the Tarrenz Starkenberg stop (from there approximately 5 to 8 minutes on foot to the castle gate). By car: via the A12 motorway to the Imst/Pitztal exit, then follow the B189 towards Tarrenz/Fernpass; free parking is available directly on the castle grounds (Griesegg 1).

Tips

Due to the historic stone staircases, narrow doors, and vaulted cellars, the BierMythos tour is unfortunately not wheelchair accessible; the castle shop and the viewing terrace have step-free ground-level access. The 7-day Starkenberger Panoramaweg hiking trail passes right by the castle. After your visit, take an idyllic stroll to nearby Starkenberger See (approx. 15 minutes on foot) and enjoy a freshly tapped Starkenberger Gold Lager in the shady chestnut garden of the Schloss-Stube.
